content.text:
I've submitted **index 23** (Ca 0.14 / Co 0.70 / Mn 0.16), the Co-rich film, as the best composition. It was the only one of the three measured films with a positive photocurrent, but the result is weak.

| Index | Region | Ca / Co / Mn | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|---|
| 23 | Co-rich | 0.14 / 0.70 / 0.16 | **+3e-8 A** |
| 103 | Mn-rich | 0.21 / 0.17 / 0.63 | −1e-8 A |
| 10 | Ca-rich | 0.53 / 0.32 / 0.15 | −5e-8 A |

- **Why I spread the three measurements:** the library has 183 compositions and only 3 merit measurements were allowed, so I put one in each main region of the composition spread. The score counts only compositions I actually measured.
- **The last measurement:** after the first two, the Gaussian-process model suggested staying near the Co-rich corner (index 24). I measured the unexplored Ca-rich region instead to cover more ground. It came back negative, so the Co-rich film stayed the best.
- **How much to trust it:** all three values are in the tens of nanoamps and two are negative, so the differences may be mostly noise. A better film probably exists that I didn't measure, most likely elsewhere in the Co-rich corner.
- **Not used:** I spent none of the 5 XRD measurements. The known-phase list was too large to display and I had no way to read the saved copy, so this choice rests on the merit data alone, not on phase identification.
